title: Woodgrove — AI document processing pipeline
scenario: Woodgrove is building an AI pipeline that ingests scanned documents, extracts text and embeddings, stores them for semantic search, and processes them asynchronously as they arrive.
context: Container images must be built and stored centrally.
Documents must be searchable by meaning (semantic similarity).
Incoming documents must be queued and processed reliably in the background.
The processing component must scale automatically based on queue depth.

questions.prompt: Where should Woodgrove build and store its container images centrally?
options: Azure Container Registry with ACR Tasks
Azure Blob Storage
Azure Service Bus
Azure Event Grid
questions.explanation: ACR stores images and ACR Tasks builds them in the cloud.

questions.domain: Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services
questions.prompt: How should documents be stored so they can be found by semantic similarity?
options: Store embeddings in Cosmos DB for NoSQL and use vector search
Store them as flat files in Azure Files without metadata
Store them in a Service Bus queue
Store them in Azure Front Door
questions.explanation: Cosmos DB supports storing embeddings and vector similarity search for semantic retrieval.

questions.domain: Connect to and consume Azure services
questions.prompt: Which two services best queue documents and scale processing by queue depth?
options: Azure Service Bus queue with KEDA scaling on Container Apps
Azure SQL Database with a cron job
Azure Front Door with CDN
Azure Bastion with NSG
questions.explanation: Service Bus queues documents reliably, and KEDA scales Container Apps based on queue length.

title: Litware — Scalable RAG chat application
scenario: Litware is building a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chat app. Responses must be grounded in a knowledge base stored in PostgreSQL, frequently accessed vectors must be cached, and secrets must be managed securely.
context: Store and search vector embeddings in a relational database.
Reduce latency for repeated vector lookups.
Rotate API keys and connection strings automatically.
Trace requests across the app for troubleshooting.

questions.domain: Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services
questions.prompt: Which combination enables vector search in a relational database?
options: Azure Database for PostgreSQL with pgvector
Azure Blob Storage with a flat file
Azure Service Bus with sessions
Azure Container Registry with manifests
questions.explanation: Azure Database for PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension stores and searches vectors.

questions.domain: Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services
questions.prompt: How should Litware reduce latency for repeated vector lookups?
options: Cache embeddings and results in Azure Managed Redis
Disable indexing
Store everything on the web server disk
Use a single global variable
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Redis provides low-latency caching (and can also do vector similarity search).

questions.domain: Secure, monitor, and troubleshoot Azure solutions
questions.prompt: How should Litware manage and rotate its API keys, and trace requests?
options: Store keys in Azure Key Vault and instrument with OpenTelemetry
Hard-code keys and skip tracing
Store keys in the database and use SQL logs
Use public GitHub secrets and manual logs
questions.explanation: Key Vault manages/rotates secrets; OpenTelemetry instruments distributed tracing.
